answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontrivial bond before it may submit jobs or vote, then slash that bond when fraud is proven through verifiable evidence and a challenge period. Because creating a thousand names does not create a thousand independent deposits, a sybil attacker must commit real capital per identity and keep it immobilized; detection can make the cost irreversible. A plume of umber accounts cannot claim haven behind cheap pseudonyms when every account has collateral at risk.
